title: The morning after he decided to close the company, he couldn’t say a word
name: Ryo Saeki
decision: He put the shutdown on hold. Once.
text: Revenue had fallen by two-thirds, and the cash would last two more months. He came in to announce the shutdown — and found his team had spent the night writing a rescue plan. Two months of cash left, and the CEO had decided to close. Faced with a rescue plan his team wrote overnight, he held back the announcement. He chose to keep the customers, not the size of the company.

title: She knew it would fail. It still took her a year to stop
name: Nao Kuroda
decision: She made herself keep her own exit rule.
text: The losses grew every month, and so did the messages from customers who believed in the product. Every signal said stop. She rewrote her own exit criteria three times. Revenue was growing, but few customers stayed past three months. Encouraging messages led her to move the exit line three times. She made the rule impossible to change alone — and closed the business.

title: He left to protect it: 143 days to walk away from the company he founded
name: Keisuke Mori
decision: He walked away from the company he built.
text: He believed nothing would move without him — until he admitted that he was the one holding the company back. Every decision ran through the founder, and the organization slowed down. Before choosing a successor, he gave up his own role. Over 143 days he handed over authority and stepped outside.
